title: BYOAIK provider descriptor
description: byoaik-1. Describes how to reach one inference provider with a user's own key. Deliberately thin: it carries only what a model catalogue structurally cannot, and defers everything else to `extends`.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, so editors can validate and autocomplete a descriptor while it is being written.

specVersion.description: Spec version. URL namespace /v1/ corresponds to byoaik-1.

id.description: Stable identifier for the provider. Never reused for a different operator.

extends.description: Advisory pointer to a models.dev provider for model-level facts. Advisory on purpose: a descriptor must remain usable if the referenced catalogue is unavailable or disagrees.

surfaces.description: Distinct API surfaces. A surface may differ by product, tenancy or geography; do not assume region.

url.description: Base URL. May contain {placeholders}, each of which must be declared in `vars`.

region.description: Serving region, when the operator states one. Absent means unknown, never assume.

vars.description: Values the setup flow must collect before the URL can be constructed.

kind.description: direct: the user's own provider key. oauth: device flow. local: no credential. scoped: a capped, revocable key. `scoped` is reserved and not implemented.

hints.description: Regexes that narrow which provider a pasted key belongs to. A hint is never authoritative: most providers issue opaque keys, so the probe decides.

jurisdiction.description: What the operator has published about where it is established and where it serves from. Reported, never inferred. A descriptor that guesses here is worse than one that says nothing.

foreignDisclosureExposure.description: Disclosure regimes the operator may be reachable by, each as an attributed assessment. Never a bare verdict: whether a regime reaches a given corporate structure is usually contested, so the entry records the facts that raise the question and a status, not legal advice.

regime.description: Extraterritorial disclosure or access regime. us-cloud-act: US CLOUD Act, compelled production regardless of storage location. us-fisa-702: US FISA Section 702, the regime Schrems II turned on. uk-investigatory-powers-act: UK IPA 2016. cn-national-intelligence-law: China NIL 2017, Article 7 cooperation duty. eu-e-evidence: EU production and preservation orders reaching providers offering services in the EU. other: not yet in this list; the basis must then name the regime precisely. Additions to this enum arrive by registry pull request.

basis.description: The published facts this status rests on.

source.description: Attribution for the claims above. Never omit.

ownership.description: Ultimate beneficial ownership, as published. operatorCountry alone is not a jurisdictional answer: a locally incorporated operator with a foreign-listed parent answers to more than its own country.

listings.description: Stock exchange listings of the parent, e.g. 'NASDAQ: NBIS'. Empty array means privately held as published; absent means not established.

notes.description: Dated, attributed observations about the jurisdictional picture, each typed by topic. Append-only in spirit: add a new note rather than rewriting an old one, so the record shows when something was learned as well as what.

topic.description: What the note is about. ownership: who ultimately controls the operator. market-entry: the operator or its parent entering a foreign market or listing. restructuring: corporate reorganisation. serving-footprint: where inference is operated from. sovereignty-commitment: published separation or residency guarantees. exposure: reasoning about a specific disclosure regime, which then requires `regime`.

regime.description: The disclosure regime an exposure note concerns.

models.description: What this provider calls each model, keyed by canonical models.dev identifier in `lab/model` form. The key names who BUILT the model; this descriptor names who SERVES it and under what string. The two are routinely different: an open-weights model is typically offered by its lab and by dozens of independent providers, each with its own routing identifier. Keying on the canonical id is what makes that many-to-many expressible instead of collapsing lab and provider into one list.

routingId.description: The exact string this provider expects in the `model` field. Case sensitive, and frequently unlike the canonical id.

alternates.description: Other deployments of the same canonical model at this provider, such as a reduced-context or higher-throughput variant. Same weights, different serving characteristics, different identifier.

surfaces.description: Surface ids this routing id was verified served on. Entitlement is per surface: the same key saw 26, 24 and 19 models on three surfaces of one provider. Absent means surface not established.

listModels.description: Request that enumerates models this key may reach, e.g. `GET /models`.

responsesApi.description: Whether the newer response-shaped endpoint is served. Not universal.

browserDirect.description: Whether the endpoint can be called directly from a browser. False means it sends no permissive CORS header, or requires an explicit opt-in header, so a client-side app needs a different route. First-class for bring-your-own-key, where the caller is often a page rather than a server.

browserNote.description: What a browser client must do when browserDirect is false.

quirks.description: Known deployment behaviours worth warning about. Hints for the probe, never a substitute for it.

verified.description: When these facts were last checked against a live endpoint, and how.
